predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: the Pyrenean valleys of Pallars, Toulousain land after Bernard II of Toulouse was assassinated in 872

successors.name: County of Pallars Jussà
successors.text: Pallars Jussà: the Tremp and Pobla de Segur side

successors.name: County of Pallars Sobirà
successors.text: Pallars Sobirà: Sort and the upper valleys

ledger.x: 872: Raymond I makes himself count of Pallars and Ribagorza.
1011: Sunyer dies and the county is divided; Raymond III takes Pallars Jussà.
1011: William II takes Pallars Sobirà in the same division ('the younger, William II, receiving Pallars Sobirà').
1011: the undivided county of Pallars ends.

wars.name: Muhammad al-Tawil's conquest of Ribagorza (907)
wars.outcome: Raymond I lost much of Ribagorza, including Roda and Montpedrós, to Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca in 907 and thereafter ruled mainly Pallars.

certainty.note: A Pyrenean valley county: the pages name valleys and towns, never a boundary line; the outline is Cliopatria's stand-in throughout.

sources.title: Raymond I of Pallars and Ribagorza
